posts.text: · Pareto:  Rating: Buy Target price (NOK): 120 Share price (NOK): 109 Odfjell Drilling UPDATE | 3 NOV 2026 CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL REPORT Still attractive cash flow ahead   ODL reported Q3 EBITDA ~3% below expectations. The miss was driven by lower utilization on some rigs, which we considered one-offs. With rates and utilization already at strong levels, upside is becoming more limited. However, at 15-16% unlevered FCF yield and 14-15% FCFE yield (after debt amort) in 2027-28e, ODL continues to offer attractive cash flow metrics, while the downside appears well protected. A sold out harsh-semi market could also provide further upside to rates. We raise our TP to NOK 120 (115) on higher estimates and reiterate BUY   Q3 EBITDA misses on lower utilization Odfjell Drilling reported Q3 EBITDA ~3% below expectations, driven by lower utilization than expected. This was primarily due to two factors, i) lower utilization on Deepsea Atlantic, due to minor start-up issues, and ii) lower utilization on Deepsea Bergen and Deepsea Aberdeen following the offshore strike earlier this summer. With September utilization at 98%, we view both effects as one-offs with limited read-through to the coming quarters. Dividends were increased to USD 0.27/share, and we expect a further increase to USD 0.3/share next quarter. We raise our estimates following the Vår Energi contract (Deepsea Bergen), the Deepsea Atlantic extension and the addition of Beacon Pacific management. Limited available supply could push rates further, but we don’t model Following Equinor’s extension of Deepsea Atlantic, and the Vår Energi contract to Deepsea Bergen, all rigs are now firm through at least 2027. The Deepsea Bergen contract at USD 475k/day (before bonuses) likely reflects the current market level and is what we model going forward. However, with the NCS (semi) fleet sold out for 2027 (only SDRL’s cold stacked West Phoenix remaining), we believe dayrates still could exceed our assumptions and provide further earnings momentum. No changes to a strong NCS outlook We see no changes to the Norwegian market outlook, with overall utilization expected to remain high. With E&P capex increasingly focused on drilling intensive infill drilling and subsea tie-backs, we expect resilient floater demand in Norway for the years ahead. ODL remains well positioned and a top pick among key clients such as Equinor, AkerBP and Vår Energi. TP lifted to NOK 120 (115) on higher estimates ODL continues to screen at the attractive end of the sector on FCF metrics. While we see a more limited upside to dayrates, downside appears well protected. Given the expected activity levels offshore Norway and limited available rig supply, we expect ODL to continue creating attractive shareholder value. We raise our TP to NOK 120 (115) on higher estimates and reiterate BUY. Our TP implies 12-13% FCFE yield (after debt amort) in 2027-28e
